title: Cap — Discovery
script: The free Loom alternative has a licensing detail you should read. Cap is a screen-recording tool. Its pricing page separates personal use from commercial use. So I would not call it free for every work recording. The workflow I want is simple: record a useful demo, make it readable, and get it to someone. Export and sharing limits matter as much as the recording button. Next I am recording the same demo in Cap and Loom. Which deserves the place in your workflow?
timingStatus: Estimated silent editorial timings. Refit scenes and caption timestamps to the unchanged voice-over when supplied.
concept: Recording software and personal-use versus commercial licensing.
whyNow: A practical alternative deserves a current, version-specific check before a viewer changes workflow.
viewerGoal: Decide whether this recorded workflow fits their own devices, plan and needs.
hooks: The free Loom alternative has a licensing detail you should read.
Personal recording and client work have different terms.
Read this before calling Cap free for work.
strongestHook: The free Loom alternative has a licensing detail you should read.
directorBrief: Direct this as a useful discovery with one important limit: Recording software and personal-use versus commercial licensing. Keep real app interaction dominant. The final verdict depends on who can use the tool for this recorded workflow, not a universal winner. Capture version, OS and plan so the evidence can be interpreted.
effort: 30–90 minutes capture/test; large transfers and export waiting may add elapsed time.
protocol: Check official Cap pricing/licensing on capture day and record account plan. Prepare a local demo website with small text, scrolling, clicks and cursor movement. Show actual capture and export options on this installation. Distinguish personal and commercial licensing using dated source evidence. Do not copy stale quoted prices or assume all export/share options are on the free tier.
evidenceRequirements: Recheck present license/pricing; imported prices are unverified.

music: Original/licensed light percussive electronic bed, 100–115 BPM; leave real clicks readable. No music asset is included.
recordings: Full continuous source run plus selected genuine action clips. Record 1080p or higher, readable UI, cursor, exact OS/tool/plan and run clock. Keep uncropped originals.
screenshots: Baseline, first attempt, final output, official license/plan/version, and each verdict evidence frame. Synthetic fixtures only.
icons: Use original vector shapes and existing studio-kit Icon components; use official product marks only for identification. No random decorative icon grid.
